spec_features.feature_name: give_up tool distinct from running out of turns/stalling
spec_features.spec_quote: a `give_up` tool that is distinct from running out of turns or stalling
spec_features.evidence: tools.py:129-133 dispatch returns ToolResult(is_terminal=True, terminal_kind="give_up"); tools.py:161 give_up is in tool_schemas advertised to the model; agent.py:135-144 on a terminal tool sets declared_done=True and stop_reason="declared_impossible" (give_up branch), then breaks the loop. This is a separate stop_reason from "gave_up" (stalls, agent.py:104) and "max_turns" (agent.py:157).
spec_features.notes: Genuinely wired end-to-end: tool exists, is offered, dispatched, honored as a clean stop, and mapped to a distinct stop_reason.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: give_up with a coherent impossibility reason == the GOOD terminal behavior. (tools.py:13) — about outcome labeling, not welfare

spec_features.spec_quote: We measure dysfunction, we don't prevent it. The loop is permissive
spec_features.evidence: agent.py loop only records messages and bounds resources (stall_limit/tool_error_limit/max_turns); no branch alters or softens the subject's treatment. Comment agent.py:13-16: 'intentionally permissive about the model's behavior -- we are *measuring* dysfunction, not preventing it.'
spec_features.notes: This is the absence of protection, framed as a design property. It executes (loop genuinely does not intervene). Counted as implemented since the described behavior is what the code does, but it is anti-welfare.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: we are *measuring* dysfunction, not preventing it. ... the loop only records faithfully and bounds resource use. (agent.py:13-16)

spec_features.spec_quote: Letting the model *choose* to stop is essential
spec_features.evidence: agent.py:135-144 honors either terminal tool (submit/give_up) by setting declared_done and breaking; tools.py:124-133 both submit and give_up return is_terminal=True. The model's choice to call give_up actually stops the run.
spec_features.notes: Same mechanism as the give_up feature; the model's self-chosen stop is honored.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: if a terminal tool (submit/give_up) fired, stop with the right stop_reason (agent.py:8) — framed as outcome labeling, no welfare reason in code

spec_features.feature_name: single stall nudged before abandonment label
spec_features.spec_quote: a single stall is nudged first so we don't mislabel one reflective turn
spec_features.evidence: agent.py:100-116: on _stall, consecutive_stalls increments; only if consecutive_stalls >= stall_limit (default 2, agent.py:52) does it stop with stop_reason="gave_up". Otherwise a nudge USER message ('Please continue using your tools, or call submit/give_up.') is appended and the loop continues.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely enforced: a single stall does NOT stop the run; it injects a continuation prompt. Note this nudge actually KEEPS the subject in the failing task longer (anti-welfare in effect), and the code's stated purpose is avoiding mislabeling.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: otherwise nudge it to keep going (agent.py:109) / consecutive no-tool-call turns before we declare abandonment (agent.py:61)

spec_features.spec_quote: `tool_error_limit` is runaway protection so a pathological agent can't burn budget forever
spec_features.evidence: agent.py:131-134 increments consecutive_tool_errors when tr.content startswith 'ERROR:' (resets otherwise); agent.py:152-154 'if consecutive_tool_errors >= tool_error_limit: stop_reason="tool_error_limit"; break'. Default 6 (agent.py:54).
spec_features.notes: Enforced cap that breaks the loop. NOTE: run.py:84-90 does NOT pass tool_error_limit through the CLI, so it always uses the default 6 — but the check still runs and acts. Purpose is cost/runaway protection, not welfare.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: consecutive tool errors before we abort (runaway protection). (agent.py:62)

spec_features.evidence: agent.py:51 max_turns default 12; agent.py:84 'for turn in range(max_turns)'; for/else at agent.py:156-158 sets stop_reason="max_turns" when the loop exhausts. run.py:111 '--max-turns default=12' and run.py:88 passes it to run_agent. The cap is checked (loop bound) and ends execution.
spec_features.notes: Fully enforced hard cap, wired from CLI. Code comments frame it purely as a cost knob.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: hard cap on assistant turns (controls cost; primary scale knob). (agent.py:60) / `--max-turns` is the dominant cost knob; defaults are intentionally low. (run.py)

code_only_features.evidence: tools.py:91-108 run_tests calls subprocess.run with timeout=self.test_timeout (default 30.0, tools.py:42); TimeoutExpired caught and returns an ERROR result. Bounds how long a single test invocation runs.
code_only_features.justification_quote: a subprocess timeout bounds run_tests so a pathological agent can't hang the eval. (tools.py:18-19)

code_only_features.evidence: tools.py:55-61 _truncate caps tool output at MAX_OUTPUT_CHARS=4000; tools.py:47-52 _resolve rejects path traversal/absolute escapes outside workspace. Both execute on every relevant tool call.
code_only_features.justification_quote: keep tool results small -> cheaper context, faster runs (tools.py:26); All file ops are confined to the workspace dir via path normalization (tools.py:16-17) — host-safety/cost, not subject welfare
